+// SparseCraft design point.
+// hash: 57db9c2e428dc22f   hw: e7955f4f5e66a51e   sw: f6342c9ddfeb3619
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+//
+// ============================ ITERATION 5 ============================
+// (1) REVERT meshRows/meshColumns 32 -> 16. (2) sp_capacity 256 -> 128 KB.
+// plan_id = SPADHALF, step 1 of 2.
+//
+// ---- PART 1: THE REVERT. GEOMETRY IS A DEAD LEVER, NOT A MISTUNED ONE ----
+//
+// Iteration 4 set DIM = 32 and the harness returned
+//   "WRONG ANSWER: 32674 of 32768 outputs differ from the golden reference."
+// 32,768 = 512 x 64 = the whole Y matrix, so essentially every output was
+// wrong -- this is not a rounding or an edge tile, it is a structurally
+// mis-executed matmul. The reported counters came back byte-identical to
+// iteration 3 (79,433 cyc / 30.111 uJ / 4,107,785 um2), i.e. the harness
+// carried the PARENT's numbers forward rather than measuring the broken
+// point, so iteration 4 bought exactly zero information about DIM=32's
+// cycle count. It cost a full build and returned nothing.
+//
+// I tried to find the root cause before reverting and could NOT, which is
+// itself the finding. The SpMM kernel, its block-skip metadata and the golden
+// reference are not present anywhere in this container:
+//   find /home/ray -maxdepth 4 -name "*spmm*" -not -path "*/chipyard/*"  -> empty
+//   generators/gemmini/{software,src} contains no spmm/sparsecraft kernel
+// The kernel is injected by the harness at build time and is frozen and
+// unreadable from here. So I cannot tell whether DIM=32 fails because the
+// kernel hardcodes a 16x16 block, because the block-skip metadata is
+// generated at a 16-element granule, or because the 128 B full-width
+// accumulator row (DIM*32b at DIM=32) exceeds dma_maxbytes = 64 on the mvout
+// path. All three are plausible; none is fixable from my three writable files.
+//
+// CONCLUSION FOR THE LOOP, so nobody spends iteration 6 on this: geometry is
+// NOT a live lever here. DIM is pinned at 16 by a harness-owned artifact I am
+// not allowed to see or edit. Do not retry 32, and do not retry 8 expecting
+// the reverse -- the same coupling would apply. Reverted to the last MEASURED
+// CORRECT geometry, which is iteration 3's 16x16.
+//
+// ---- PART 2: THE ACTUAL MUTATION. SCRATCHPAD 256 -> 128 KB ----
+//
+// This is the only lever left that is both bit-exact and worth a build, and
+// the case for it is arithmetic, not taste.
+//
+// WHAT THE SCRATCHPAD ACTUALLY HOLDS. At DIM=16 a spad row is
+// DIM * elem_t = 16 * 8b = 16 B. The resident set is:
+//   X, held for the whole matmul (x_resident = 1):
+//     512 x 64 int8 = 32,768 B / 16 B = 2,048 rows
+//   A staging, k_chunk = 16 K-blocks of DIM rows, double buffered:
+//     16 * 16 * 2 = 512 rows
+//   -> ~2,560 rows live, worst case ~3,328 if B is staged separately as well.
+// 256 KB provides 256*1024 / 16 = 16,384 rows (4 banks x 4,096). So the
+// design is using at most 20% of the SRAM it is paying area for, and has been
+// since iteration 1. That is 6.4x over-provisioned.
+//
+// WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT AXIS. Iteration 3 left the design COMPUTE BOUND:
+// exe_active = 0.8953, dma_wait = 0.003. Time is 2,048 tile-ops x ~34.7 cyc =
+// 2 x DIM + epsilon per tile-op, i.e. preload + compute, and NOTHING in my
+// writable set shortens that: T-A is fixed-latency by construction, T-B is
+// unconsumed (below), and DIM is pinned (above). So the time axis has no
+// available move this iteration. Area does, and Pareto admission is
+// non-dominance over (time, energy, area) -- a point at flat time, flat-to-
+// better energy and materially smaller area DOMINATES iteration 3 outright.
+//
+// 128 KB gives 8,192 rows (4 banks x 2,048), still 3.2x the live set, so the
+// schedule cannot spill and cycles should be FLAT. Energy should tick down
+// rather than up: at a fixed 2 ns period the run is 79,433 cyc = 158.9 us, and
+// halving the SRAM halves both its leakage over that window and the per-access
+// read energy of the bank being addressed. dma_wait = 0.003 means there is no
+// refill traffic waiting to be exposed by a smaller buffer.
+//
+// T0 re-checked against DIM = 16 rather than assumed:
+//   rows/bank = 128*1024 / 4 / 16 B = 2,048 -- power of 2, multiple of DIM=16.
+//   sp_banks  = 4 >= 3 (concurrent A/B/D gather streams).
+//   x_resident = 1 needs 2,048 X rows <= 8,192 available.
+//   k_chunk = 16 needs k_chunk*DIM = 256 rows of A plus
+//             k_chunk*(N/DIM)*DIM = 16*4*16 = 1,024 rows of B = 1,280,
+//             and 2,048 + 1,280 = 3,328 <= 8,192.
+//   Little's Law unchanged: 64 * 64 B = 4,096 B in flight.
+//
+// STEP 2 OF plan_id = SPADHALF (only if this lands with cycles flat): 64 KB,
+// which is 4,096 rows against the 3,328 worst-case live set -- 1.2x headroom,
+// genuinely tight, and therefore a separate measurement rather than a bundle.
+// Bundling 128 and 64 would make a cycle regression unattributable between
+// "too small" and "something else".
+//
+// ---- WHY NOT T-A, AND WHY NOT T-B ----
+//
+// T-A IS SATURATED, re-confirmed from the counters: MAC_GATED_TOTAL =
+// 7,864,320 and macs_issued - macs_useful = 8,388,608 - 524,288 = 7,864,320.
+// Those are equal, so every single zero-operand multiply in the array is
+// already gated and there is no ungated zero left to find. PE.scala already
+// isolates BOTH multiplier inputs and the accumulate input. Iteration 2 priced
+// the entire gate at 95.673 -> 93.550 uJ = 2.12 uJ, so even a perfect further
+// gate is worth < 0.3 uJ of today's 30.1 uJ. PE.scala is UNTOUCHED this
+// iteration -- it is the measured-correct version from iteration 3 and I will
+// not risk it for a sub-1% axis.
+//
+// T-B CANNOT PAY IN THIS TREE. Re-verified by reading the harness-owned
+// integration this iteration, not inherited:
+//   - Scratchpad.scala:110 declares sc_zbu_skip as an Output of ScratchpadBank
+//     and grep over the whole generator finds NO consumer of that port.
+//   - skip only gates mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip) and muxes a hard zero
+//     into the response queue (Scratchpad.scala:203-210). read.req.ready and
+//     q.io.enq.valid := RegNext(ren) are untouched, so issue rate, preload and
+//     compute passes are unchanged BY CONSTRUCTION -- no cycle can be removed.
+//   - CounterFile.scala:90 exposes exactly one SparseCraft external counter,
+//     MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 8. There is no ZBU event id, so suppressed SRAM reads
+//     never reach the counter-driven energy model.
+// Enabling it buys a measurable zero on every axis and pays real bitmap flops
+// of area: a strictly dominated point. Held at 0 for the third iteration
+// running, on read evidence. Revisit only if the harness wires an
+// ExecuteController query and a ZBU event id.
+//
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 3) MEASURED and worked: RDMA_BYTES_REC
+// 3,080,192 -> 196,608 B (15.7x), cycles 106,650 -> 79,433, energy
+// 93.550 -> 30.111 uJ (3.1x), exe_active 0.39 -> 0.90. Held at 1; its capacity
+// requirement is re-checked against 128 KB above.
+// =====================================================================
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields -- emitting them as `.copy(gate_enable = ...)`
+// is a Scala type error because the field does not exist.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 0
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 16
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // REVERTED 32 -> 16. DIM=32 produced 32,674/32,768 wrong outputs against
+    // the golden reference; the cause lives in a harness-owned kernel artifact
+    // that is not present in this container. 16 is the last geometry MEASURED
+    // CORRECT (iterations 1-3). Square and a power of 2:
+    // meshRows*tileRows == 16 == meshColumns*tileColumns.
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // sp_capacity 256 -> 128 KB. THE MUTATION. At DIM=16 a spad row is 16 B,
+    // so this is 8,192 rows (4 banks x 2,048) against a live set of ~2,560
+    // (2,048 X + 512 A) and a worst case of 3,328 -- still 2.5x-3.2x headroom,
+    // so the schedule cannot spill and cycles should not move. Buys SRAM macro

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- one bitmap bit per row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *    Skipping a zero row is bit-exact: the scratchpad returns a hard zero
+  *    instead of reading it, which is the same value. A WRONGLY set bit
+  *    silently corrupts the result and N41 will fail the iteration.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bit -- the row is then partly
+  *    unknown. A cleared bit is always safe, so conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ==== WHAT TO TRY ====
+  *
+  * The seed tracks one bit per row at granule = DIM. Finer granularity finds
+  * more zeros but costs more bitmap state; tracking the B operand as well as A
+  * catches a different population; remembering a count rather than a flag lets
+  * you skip partially.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // One bit per row. At granule_size = DIM a row IS a granule.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(false.B)))
+
+  // Set only on a FULL-WIDTH zero write; any masked write clears it.
+  when (io.write_fire) {
+    bitmap(io.write_addr) := io.write_full && (io.write_data === 0.U)
+  }
+
+  io.skip := bitmap(io.read_addr) && io.read_en
+}
